description: What environment.preflight found, as data: one record per readiness check and one per wall. The Checks table of the environment-readiness receipt and `checks` agree one-to-one by id and status; every `wall` check has exactly one entry in `walls`. The check vocabulary is closed and lives in `$defs.checkIds`: the validator expands `<role>` over the requested roles and `<class>` over the operation classes the environment schema publishes, and the id set of a report equals that expansion exactly, so a check that was not run is visible as a missing id and never as silence. A check's family is the first segment of its id. Two checks are read back from the host by the validator rather than taken from the report: the approval checks against the declaration on disk, and host.playwright against the install scripts/browser-walk.mjs would load.

flow.description: The flow whose account record and sign-in were probed; null when the request named none, in which case the identity.flow checks are skipped.

declarationRef.description: The environment declaration the approval checks were read from, as its path from the host repository root and the sha256 of its bytes; null when the environment declares nothing, in which case every approval check is a wall.

evidence.description: What was observed: an outcome, a name, a length or a digest; never a credential value, which the response gate sweeps for.

owner.description: Who clears the wall; null for a check that is ok or skipped.

repair.description: What clears the wall. A declaration wall whose requested name is a near match of one declaration names it as suggested `<id>`, and that phrase is what makes ROUTE_NAME_NEAR_MATCH a taken fallback.

checkIds.description: The closed vocabulary of checks, one template per readiness question. `<role>` expands over the requested roles, `<class>` over the operation classes the environment schema publishes under authorization. declaration: the portable declaration exists and its hydrated route projects it. checkout: the route carries a git policy, the tree is clean, the branch is one the policy permits. identity: the sealed admin credential preflight, and the flow's account record and sign-in probe when a flow is named. runtime: the registry entry of the route, the served head containing the bound head, the projected port answering, and no foreign process holding it. host: a browser binary for the audit profile, the host's Playwright install for @tools/browsercontrol mode playwright (present where resources/tools.json → browsercontrol.install says, with a Chromium under its browsers path), a reachable container daemon, installed dependencies per checkout, and no ancestor node_modules leaking types into the checkout's typecheck. approval: who authorises each operation class.
